title: 80,000 ka phone No Cost EMI pe: kitna extra lagta hai?
hooks: Raghav ne 80 hazaar ka phone No Cost EMI pe liya.
No Cost EMI pe phone lene se pehle ye hisab dekh lo.
Assi hazar ke phone pe No Cost EMI ka asli bill kitna hai?
hook_why: Relatable scenario hook naming a person, the exact phone cost, and the topic in the first 5 words.
metaphor: Zero interest discount banner hiding bank processing fee and monthly GST stamps underneath.
mechanism: RBI circular says zero percent interest loans are invalid; interest is hidden in invoice discount
Merchant discounts invoice by the interest amount, bank runs a standard loan on that discounted price
Bank charges a one-time processing fee (like a file charge) plus 18% GST upfront
Government levies 18% GST on the interest portion of every monthly EMI
Buyer loses the instant card discount on full payment and the full purchase amount blocks the credit limit

caption:
Raghav ne ₹80,000 ka phone No Cost EMI pe liya, par asli kharcha kitna hua?

RBI ke 2013 circular ke mutabiq zero percent interest loan valid nahi hai. Merchant interest discount deta hai, par bank loan par processing fee + 18% GST upfront lagata hai. Har mahine interest portion par 18% GST lagta hai. Saath hi full payment par milne wala instant card discount bhi nahi milta aur poora amount credit limit block karta hai.

Source: RBI circular DBOD.No.Dir.BC.47/13.03.00/2013-14 dated 17 Sep 2013; Bank EMI schedules; CGST Act 2017.

claims.claim: RBI prohibited zero percent interest loan schemes without genuine restructuring in 2013
Banks charge an EMI conversion processing fee plus 18% GST on that fee
claims.basis: Standard major Indian credit card EMI schedule of charges (HDFC, ICICI, SBI Card)

claims.claim: 18% GST is levied on the interest component of No Cost EMIs
claims.basis: Section 15 of CGST Act 2017 & Indian bank consumer lending T&Cs on subvention EMIs

claims.claim: Retailers offer instant discount on upfront full card payment which is not available on EMI subvention
claims.basis: Amazon India and Flipkart electronics sale pricing terms

claims.claim: The full purchase amount blocks the credit card limit, not just the EMI amount
claims.basis: Credit card limit mechanics per RBI master direction on credit card operations

steps_learned: RBI's stance that 0% interest is not a reality in the banking system
The mechanism where the retailer provides a discount equal to the interest amount to the bank
The application of a processing fee (file charge) by the bank at the start
The addition of 18% GST on the processing fee and the monthly interest component
The trade-off where you lose the benefit of instant upfront card discounts
The blocking of the full purchase amount (80,000) against the credit card limit
missing_steps: The specific calculation of how the 'interest' is hidden within the 'discount' amount
The impact on the credit score if an EMI is missed
Pre-payment or foreclosure charges if one wants to close the loan early
